name: Slow Cooker Pork and Sauerkraut with Apples and Potatoes
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Sauerkraut, apples and apple-juice are all board commodities, making this one of the cheapest pork dinners in the slice. Source verified at 267 cal / 38g protein per serving over 8 servings for the pork and kraut; add mashed or roasted potatoes and it lands 500-550 cal with an outstanding protein ratio. New Year's Day Midwest staple, nothing like it in the catalog. | HARVEST: Source list contains no potatoes; the target recipe's potato component is not in this source.
intro_html: Across the Midwest, pork and sauerkraut on New Year's Day is not a suggestion, it is a rule. The pig roots forward, the story goes, so you eat pork to move forward in the new year. Apples and apple juice are what keep the kraut from being harsh, cooking down into something sweet and tangy at the same time. The slow cooker does all of it while you do nothing, and it comes out of the crock at the end of the day tender enough to shred.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 5.75 cups dry: ~$1.28. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Pantry seasonings (black pepper, salt): ~$0.35. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $17.41 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.24 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $21.91 across 14 servings, roughly $1.56 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $9.44 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $31.35. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.02 a bowl (at everyday cost). Sauerkraut, apples and apple juice are all inexpensive, and pork loin on sale finishes the job.
shop_smart: Canned sauerkraut is the value buy. The refrigerated jars cost more and this recipe cooks the kraut for hours anyway, so the shelf stable cans do exactly the same work for less.
Watch for whole pork loin on sale and cut it down yourself. A whole loin runs well under the price of precut roasts or chops, and it freezes in portions beautifully.
Apple juice is the cheapest braising liquid in the store. One bottle covers this batch and it does more for the flavor than an equal amount of broth would.
Rinse the kraut if you like it mild. A quick rinse in a colander takes the sharp edge off for free, and lets the apple sweetness come forward.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the pork loin dry, season it all over with salt and black pepper, and sear it in the vegetable oil in a hot skillet until the outside is browned on every side.
Lay the sliced onion in the bottom of the slow cooker and set the seared pork on top of it.
Drain the sauerkraut, rinse it if you prefer it mild, and pile it around and over the pork along with the minced garlic.
Core and slice the apples and tuck them in around the edges, then pour the apple juice over everything.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours, until the pork pulls apart easily with a fork.
Shred the pork right in the crock so it takes the juices back up, and cook the rice per the package to serve underneath.
portion_html: Spread the cooked rice across your 14 containers, then set your mixing pot of pork and kraut on the scale, subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1, divide by 14, and spoon that exact weight over the rice. Every serving lands near 562 calories with 42 grams of protein, which is a strong protein number for a dollar and change.

head.description: Pork loin slow cooked with sauerkraut, apples and apple juice until it shreds, served over rice. A 14 serving Midwest classic built for cheap meal prep.
head.keywords: pork and sauerkraut, slow cooker pork loin, new years day pork, apple pork recipe, budget meal prep, cheap dinner ideas
steps: Season and sear the pork loin on all sides.
Layer sliced onion in the slow cooker and set the pork on top.
Add the drained sauerkraut, garlic and sliced apples around the pork.
Pour in the apple juice and cook on low 7 to 8 hours.
Shred the pork in the crock and serve over cooked rice.
